title: How Malaria Carved Sickle-Cell Genes Into Human Blood and Proved Evolution in Action — Pauling's pH 8.6 Hemoglobin Electrophoresis, Allison's 1954 Ugandan Cohort, Wright–Haldane Balancing Selection (q* = 15%) & BCL11A CRISPR HbF

teenKit.tldr: Malaria acted as a brutal evolutionary pressure, carving the sickle-cell gene into human blood as a lifesaving trade-off against a deadly parasite. Today, science is using revolutionary tools like CRISPR to rewrite that ancient compromise.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Understanding how our DNA adapted to ancient diseases proves that evolution is happening right inside our bodies, shaping modern medicine and gene therapies that can cure inherited disorders.
keyTakeaways: Walter Clement Noelle's 1910 case in Chicago helped reveal sickle-cell anemia, turning it into the first molecular disease ever discovered.
Anthony Allison's 1954 Ugandan cohort proved that carrying one copy of the sickle-cell gene protects people from dying of malaria.
Balancing selection creates a genetic sweet spot where keeping a harmful mutation alive prevents an even deadlier infection in a specific environment.

vocab.meaning: A laboratory technique used by Linus Pauling that separates different types of proteins in the blood using an electric field based on their electrical charge.
An evolutionary process where natural selection maintains multiple versions of a gene in a population because the hybrid combination provides a survival advantage.
The scientific study of ancient diseases and medical conditions using historical remains, bones, and genetic evidence from the deep past.
A breakthrough gene-editing technology that allows scientists to precisely target, cut, and modify DNA sequences inside living cells.

quiz.question: Why did the sickle-cell gene persist in human populations despite causing severe health problems?
options: It gave people supernatural physical strength.
It offered partial protection against deadly malaria infections.
It completely stopped people from catching any virus.
It was purely a random accident with no biological benefit.
quiz.explanation: Carrying a single copy of the sickle-cell trait disrupts the malaria parasite's ability to infect red blood cells, saving lives in malaria-prone regions.

quiz.question: What did Linus Pauling's pH 8.6 hemoglobin electrophoresis accomplish?
options: It invented the very first malaria vaccine.
It proved that diseases are caused exclusively by cold weather.
It identified sickle-cell anemia as the first-ever molecular disease by showing structural differences in protein charge.
It mapped out the entire human genome for the first time.
quiz.explanation: Pauling used electrophoresis to show that normal hemoglobin and sickle-cell hemoglobin moved differently in an electric field due to a molecular difference.

quiz.question: What role does modern BCL11A CRISPR technology play in relation to sickle-cell disease?
options: It edits genes to reactivate fetal hemoglobin, offering a potential genetic cure for the disease.
It spreads malaria faster among human populations.
It completely stops the human body from producing any red blood cells.
quiz.explanation: CRISPR targets the BCL11A gene to turn fetal hemoglobin back on, which compensates for the defective adult hemoglobin found in sickle-cell patients.
